title: Counit identification of a scalar support-triangle comparison
statement:
Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow P$ be a closed immersion with complementary open $j:U\hookrightarrow P$, and let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Use ordinary etale module derived categories, the support triangles $i_*Ri_R^!L\to L\to Rj_{*,R}j^*L$ for $R=A,B$, and their counit/unit maps [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]. Write $T_W=-\otimes_A^LB_W$ and $\operatorname{Res}$ for exact restriction of scalars [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Let $L$ and $TL$, their closed exceptional images and the open terms in these triangles all be bounded below. Suppose the canonical projection $q_{i,Ri_A^!L}:T_Pi_{*,A}Ri_A^!L\to i_{*,B}T_ZRi_A^!L$ is an isomorphism. Suppose a morphism from the restriction $\operatorname{Res}(T_P(-))$ of the $A$-support triangle to the restriction of the $B$-support triangle has middle map the identity of $\operatorname{Res}(TL)$ and right map the canonical open coefficient projection. Identify its first source term using $\operatorname{Res}(q_i)$ and the canonical restriction/direct-image isomorphisms [lem-sbc-canonical-restrict-scalars-functor-comparisons]. Then its first map is $i_*\operatorname{Res}(b_i)$, where
$$b_i:T_ZRi_A^!L\to Ri_B^!T_PL$$
is the $i_{*,B}\dashv Ri_B^!$ transpose of $T_P\epsilon_{i,A}\circ q_i^{-1}$. If the open coefficient projection is an isomorphism, then $b_i$ is an isomorphism. No injectivity after restriction of scalars and no flatness of $B/A$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use the actual coefficient adjunction scalarExtension adjoint derivedRestrictScalars. Additivity of its right adjoint gives additivity of scalar extension. Equip scalar extension with the published adjunction-compatible shift structure; the adjoint of exact restriction is triangulated. Thus scalar extension followed by restriction preserves the A-support triangle, and restriction preserves the B-support triangle.

Put M=Ri_A!K, q=(scalarMate phi i)_M, b=scalarSupportClosedMate phi i K, and RP=derived restriction on P. The inverse Hom equivalence for i_*B adjoint Ri_B! gives i_*B(b);epsilon_B=q^(-1);T(epsilon_A). Apply RP and precompose with RP(q). The result has the same composite with RP(epsilon_B) as tau.hom1, by the first square and tau.hom2=1.

Let E=i_*A M and S=Res_P(T_P E). Disjointness gives Lj_A* E=0. The canonical scalar/pullback isomorphism gives Lj_B*(T_P E)=0, and the exact restriction/pullback isomorphism gives Lj_A* S=0. Commutation with shifts gives Lj_A*(S[1])=0. Apply the scalar/pullback isomorphism again to obtain Lj_B*(T_P(S[1]))=0. Compose T_P adjoint Res_P with Lj_B* adjoint Rj_*B. It identifies Hom_A(S[1],Res_P Rj_*B N) with Hom_B(Lj_B*T_P(S[1]),N), a subsingleton for every N. This avoids any direct-image/restriction comparison or boundedness requirement.

Apply Triangle.cancel_mor1_of_subsingleton to the restricted B-support triangle and Step 3, with N=j_B*T_PK. This is the Hom exactness cancellation lemma: the difference factors through the negative shift of the third vertex and vanishes. The equal counit composites from Step 2 imply tau.hom1=RP(q);RP(i_*B(b)). Naturality of scalarRestrictionDirectImageMap at b proves the transported equality without needing that comparison to be invertible.

If the open coefficient projection is invertible, tau.hom2 and tau.hom3 are invertible. Triangle two-of-three makes tau.hom1 invertible. The identification in Step 4 and invertibility of RP(q) make RP(i_*B(b)) invertible.

Exact restriction commutes with all derived homology functors. Since sheaf restriction reflects isomorphisms, the unbounded derived homology criterion shows it reflects isomorphisms too. Hence i_*B(b) is invertible. Closed direct image is fully faithful on sheaves and preserves K-injectives; its total right derived functor is fully faithful and therefore reflects isomorphisms. Consequently b is invertible. This avoids descending the closed inverse/direct-image counit through restriction.

proof_origin.place: Existence and Locality; coefficient adjunction and scalar/pullback transport give supported/open orthogonality directly. The existing cancellation lemma, triangle two-of-three, homology conservativity and fully faithful derived closed direct image complete the proof.

Nothing is weakened, and the report names the change. Step checks: (1) T is triangulated by derived-change-of-rings (2), Res is exact and termwise, and the unbounded support triangles over any finite ring give e∘a=s. (2) The closed-ambient transpose gives e∘h=s. (3) Res i_*=i_* Res termwise (exact i_* from the trf closed-subtopos node, plus the factorization lemma), so this holds even for unbounded T_Z M. That gives j^*S=0. The open term goes through the D+ sbc comparison, which is valid because j^*TL is bounded below. So Hom(S[1],O)=0 by j^*⊣Rj_*. (4) Hom-exactness on the rotated triangle gives a=h. The target identification is via sbc (N is bounded below by hypothesis). (5) Two-of-three on the full triangle morphism. (6) i^*i_*≅1 termwise, then descended. (7) Res commutes with H^r and reflects module isomorphisms, then the cohomological iso criterion applies. Tested i=id, Z empty, A=B, and non-flat Z/4→Z/2 (unbounded T_Z M is handled termwise).
